body.en: Functions describe deterministic mathematical relationships between inputs and outputs. On the ACT, questions examine function notation, domain and range restrictions, composite functions, inverse operations, and graphical transformations.

label.en: ● Level 1 Foundation — Function Notation, Domain & Range Restrictions

body.en:
A function \(f\) assigns to each input \(x\) in its domain exactly one output \(f(x)\) in its range. The vertical line test states that a curve in the coordinate plane represents a function if and only if every vertical line intersects the curve at most once.

Core Domain Restrictions on the ACT:

  • Fractions: Denominators cannot equal zero: \(f(x) = \frac{1}{g(x)} \implies g(x) \neq 0\).
  • Even Radicals: Radicands under square roots cannot be negative in the real number system: \(f(x) = \sqrt{g(x)} \implies g(x) \ge 0\).
  • Logarithms: Arguments must be strictly positive: \(f(x) = \log_b(g(x)) \implies g(x) > 0\).

Piecewise Functions: Evaluated by determining which interval contains the input \(x\) and applying the corresponding sub-function rule.

label.en: ● Level 2 Analytical Tools — Composite Functions, Inverses & Transformations

body.en:
Composite Functions: The composite \((f \circ g)(x) = f(g(x))\) is evaluated from the inside out: calculate \(g(x)\) first, then substitute that output value as the input for \(f\). In general, \(f(g(x)) \neq g(f(x))\).

Inverse Functions \(f^{-1}(x)\): An inverse exists if and only if \(f\) passes the horizontal line test (one-to-one). To find the inverse algebraically:

  1. Replace \(f(x)\) with \(y\).
  2. Interchange the variables \(x\) and \(y\).
  3. Solve explicitly for \(y\) in terms of \(x\).

Geometrically, the graph of \(y = f^{-1}(x)\) is the reflection of \(y = f(x)\) across the line \(y = x\).

Function Transformations \(y = a f(x - h) + k\):

  • Horizontal Shift \(h\): \(f(x - h)\) shifts the graph right by \(h\) units; \(f(x + h)\) shifts it left by \(h\) units.
  • Vertical Shift \(k\): \(f(x) + k\) shifts up by \(k\); \(f(x) - k\) shifts down by \(k\).
  • Vertical Stretch/Reflection: \(a f(x)\) stretches vertically by factor \(|a|\). If \(a < 0\), the curve reflects across the \(x\)-axis.
  • Horizontal Reflection: \(f(-x)\) reflects the curve across the \(y\)-axis.
Slide the vertex \( (h,k) \) of \( y=(x-h)^{2}+k \). The amber dot is the vertex; the dashed line is the axis of symmetry.

label.en: ● Level 3 ACT Mastery — Quadratic Vertex Form, Optimization & Rates of Change

body.en:
Quadratic Parabola Formulations:

  • Vertex Form: \[ y = a(x - h)^2 + k. \] The vertex is \((h, k)\) and the vertical axis of symmetry is \(x = h\). If \(a > 0\), the parabola opens upwards and has a minimum value of \(k\); if \(a < 0\), it opens downwards and has a maximum value of \(k\).
  • Standard Form Conversion: For \(y = ax^2 + bx + c\), the \(x\)-coordinate of the vertex is: \[ h = -\frac{b}{2a}, \quad k = f\left(-\frac{b}{2a}\right). \]
  • Factored Form: \(y = a(x - p)(x - q)\). The \(x\)-intercepts are \(p\) and \(q\), and the axis of symmetry lies exactly halfway between them: \(h = \frac{p + q}{2}\).

Average Rate of Change: The average rate of change of \(f(x)\) over an interval \([a, b]\) is the slope of the secant line:

\[ \text{Average Rate of Change} = \frac{f(b) - f(a)}{b - a}. \]

• Order of Composition: \( (f \circ g)(x) = f(g(x)) \) means evaluate \( g(x) \) FIRST, then substitute the result into \( f \). Evaluating outside-in is one of the most common ACT distractor answer choices.
  • Domain Restrictions: Watch for two key restrictions: denominators cannot equal zero (e.g., \( \frac{1}{x-3} \implies x \neq 3 \)), and expressions under an even radical cannot be negative (e.g., \( \sqrt{2x-8} \implies 2x-8 \ge 0 \implies x \ge 4 \)).
  • Vertical Line Test vs. Horizontal Line Test: A vertical line tests whether a graph is a function (each input has at most one output). A horizontal line tests whether a function is one-to-one (has an invertible function \( f^{-1}(x) \)).
  • Function Transformations: \( f(x - c) \) shifts RIGHT by \( c \), while \( f(x + c) \) shifts LEFT by \( c \) (horizontal operations are counter-intuitive). Vertical shifts \( f(x) + c \) go UP, and \( f(x) - c \) go DOWN.

label.en: ◆ Why It Works — First-Principles Derivation (Functions & Graphs)

body.en:
Why Completing the Square & Log-Linearization Work: Any quadratic \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\) (\(a \ne 0\)) can be rewritten by factoring \(a\) from the first two terms and adding/subtracting \((b/2a)^2\):

\[ ax^2 + bx + c = a\!\left(x + \frac{b}{2a}\right)^2 + \left(c - \frac{b^2}{4a}\right) \]

Because \(\left(x + \frac{b}{2a}\right)^2 \ge 0\) for all \(x \in \mathbb{R}\), the extreme value \(k = c - \frac{b^2}{4a}\) is attained uniquely at the axis of symmetry \(x = -\frac{b}{2a}\), restricting the range to \([k, \infty)\) (if \(a > 0\)) and making \(f\) invertible on \(x \ge -\frac{b}{2a}\). Similarly, applying \(\ln\) to power laws \(y = ax^n\) yields \(\ln y = n\ln x + \ln a\), transforming a nonlinear curve into a straight line of gradient \(n\).

problem.en:
Let \(f(x) = x^2 - 4\) and \(g(x) = \sqrt{2x + 1}\).
(a) Find the domain of \(g(x)\).
(b) Evaluate \((f \circ g)(4)\).
(c) Find an algebraic expression for \((g \circ f)(x)\).

solution.en:
(a) The radicand must be non-negative: \(2x + 1 \ge 0 \implies 2x \ge -1 \implies x \ge -0.5\). Domain: \([-0.5, \infty)\).

(b) Evaluate inside first: \(g(4) = \sqrt{2(4) + 1} = \sqrt{9} = 3\).
Substitute into \(f\): \(f(3) = 3^2 - 4 = 9 - 4 = 5\).
Thus \((f \circ g)(4) = 5\).

(c) Substitute \(f(x)\) as the input to \(g\):
\[ (g \circ f)(x) = g(x^2 - 4) = \sqrt{2(x^2 - 4) + 1} = \sqrt{2x^2 - 8 + 1} = \sqrt{2x^2 - 7}. \]

label.en: Worked Example 3.2 — Quadratic Maximum in Word Context

problem.en: A farmer has 120 feet of fencing to enclose a rectangular pen against an existing stone barn (no fencing is needed along the side against the barn). If the pen has width \(x\) feet perpendicular to the barn, what value of \(x\) maximizes the area of the pen, and what is the maximum area?

solution.en:
1. The fencing covers two widths \(x\) and one length \(L\):
\[ 2x + L = 120 \implies L = 120 - 2x. \]

2. Form the area function \(A(x)\):
\[ A(x) = x \cdot L = x(120 - 2x) = 120x - 2x^2 = -2x^2 + 120x. \]

3. This is a parabola opening downwards with \(a = -2\) and \(b = 120\).
The maximum occurs at the vertex:
\[ x = -\frac{b}{2a} = -\frac{120}{2(-2)} = -\frac{120}{-4} = 30\text{ feet}. \]

4. Compute the maximum area:
\[ A(30) = -2(30^2) + 120(30) = -2(900) + 3600 = -1800 + 3600 = 1800\text{ ft}^2. \]

The optimal width is 30 feet and the maximum area is 1,800 ft².

label.en: Worked Example 4.C — Piecewise Function Evaluation at Boundary Inputs

body.en:
Let \(f(x) = \begin{cases} 2x^2 - 1 & x < 2 \\ 5x - 3 & x \geq 2 \end{cases}\). Compute \(f(-1) + f(2)\).

Solution: Since \(-1 < 2\), \(f(-1) = 2(-1)^2 - 1 = 1\). Since \(2 \geq 2\), \(f(2) = 5(2) - 3 = 7\). Thus \(f(-1) + f(2) = 1 + 7 = \mathbf{8}\).

label.en: Worked Example 4.D — Vertical & Horizontal Asymptotes of Rational Functions

body.en:
Find the vertical and horizontal asymptotes of \(g(x) = \frac{6x - 5}{2x + 4}\).

Solution: Set denominator to zero for the vertical asymptote: \(2x + 4 = 0 \implies \mathbf{x = -2}\). Since numerator and denominator have equal degree \(1\), the horizontal asymptote is the ratio of leading coefficients: \(y = \frac{6}{2} = \mathbf{3}\).

caption.en: Error Diagnosis — Common Student Traps vs. Exam-Board Method (Functions & Graphs)

rows.en: Confuses the product law \(\ln(xy) = \ln x + \ln y\) with a non-existent sum rule.
Only factor products, quotients, and powers inside logarithms: \(\ln(xy) = \ln x + \ln y\).
Keeping both roots of \(\sqrt{2x+5} = x - 1\) without checking \(x - 1 \ge 0\)
Squaring both sides loses the sign of \(x - {r}\), introducing roots where \(\sqrt{\cdot} = -\text{number}\).
Enforce the range condition \(x \ge 1\) before or after squaring.
Restricting domain of \(f(x) = (x-3)^2 + 1\) to \(x \ge 0\) for invertibility
The vertex is at \(x = 3\), so \(f(2) = f(4) = 2\) fails the horizontal line test on \(x \ge 0\).
Restrict the domain at the vertex axis of symmetry: \(x \ge 3\) (or \(x \le 3\)).

label.en: ▲ Exam Pacing & Verification Strategy — Functions & Graphs

body.en: Fast Exam Check (ACT Mathematics Test): To verify an inverse function \(f^{-1}(x)\) in 5 seconds, pick a simple input \(x_0\), compute \(y_0 = f(x_0)\), and check that \(f^{-1}(y_0) = x_0\). Also verify that the graph of \(y = f^{-1}(x)\) reflects \(y = f(x)\) across \(y = x\).

question.en: Practice 3.2: What is the domain of the function \(f(x) = \dfrac{\sqrt{x + 5}}{x - 3}\)?

solution.en:
For the radical in the numerator to be defined, the radicand must be non-negative: \(x + 5 \ge 0 \implies x \ge -5\).
For the rational expression to be defined, the denominator cannot equal zero: \(x - 3 eq 0 \implies x eq 3\).
Combining both restrictions gives \(x \ge -5\) and \(x eq 3\), or in interval notation \([-5, 3) \cup (3, \infty)\).

hints.en: For the radical in the numerator to be defined, the radicand must be non-negative: \(x + 5 \ge 0 \implies x \ge -5\).
For the rational expression to be defined, the denominator cannot equal zero: \(x - 3 \neq 0 \implies x \neq 3\).
Combining both restrictions gives \(x \ge -5\) and \(x \neq 3\), or in interval notation \([-5, 3) \cup (3, \infty)\).
Evaluate \(5^2 + 2\) to obtain the final answer.
